name: Graves

rules.yield_base: 55 hl/ha for red, 58 for dry white, 40 for sweet white

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
keyfacts: Graves is named for its gravelly soils, carried by the Garonne from Pyrenean valleys, and forms a band about ten kilometers wide on the river's left bank from north of Bordeaux to southeast of Langon.
Sixteen châteaux were classified in the 1959 Crus Classés de Graves, all within what is now Pessac-Léognan.
In 1987 the part closest to the city of Bordeaux became a separate AOC, Pessac-Léognan, home of first growth Château Haut-Brion.
Graves AOC covers red, dry white and sweet white wines, and the sweet whites may use the name Graves Supérieures only up to the 2028 harvest.

notes: Its oak-aged dry Sauvignon Blanc blends are among the few Sauvignons that age well.
Sauternes and Cérons, inside Graves, make sweet whites shaped by noble rot.

blurb.text: A Bordeaux sub-region on the left bank of the Garonne, with red and white wines, mostly red. Reds blend Cabernet and Merlot, and whites use Sauvignon, Sémillon and Muscadelle. The name means gravelly land.
